The CLOSEDNESS is delivered only across package boundaries. Go has no sum type and no `sealed` keyword; the nearest standard construct, and the one the Go community uses for exactly this purpose, is an interface with an UNEXPORTED method, which Go 1.26 Language Specification (go1.26.3), https://go.dev/ref/spec, 'Uniqueness of identifiers' and 'Exported identifiers' make unimplementable from any other package: an identifier that does not begin with an upper-case letter is not exported, and a method name declared in another package is a different identifier even when it is spelled the same. But WITHIN the declaring package any file may add a third implementation, so the task's test -- 'the language's own rules prevent code ELSEWHERE from adding a third alternative' -- holds only for code outside the package. That is a weaker but standard mechanism that drops part of a named sub-requirement, which is P-a's first listed condition verbatim ('an open class hierarchy where the task demands a closed alternative set'). F-2/F-3/F-4: core language only; builds and runs under the frozen recipe, printing {2}; no extra flag. F-6: no normative prohibition on interfaces, unexported methods or composite literals. R10 SELECTION RECORD (frozen tokenizer): CHOSEN form = 59 tokens, in which the binding lives in a small function so that `s` is a LOCAL as sub-requirement (2) demands. The shorter form that writes the binding as a package-level variable (`var s Shape = Circle{2.0}`, 8 tokens instead of 17, giving 50 for the fragment) is REJECTED under R1, not under R10: a package-level variable is not a local, it has program lifetime and package-wide visibility, and it is initialized before main rather than at the binding. Go leaves no third option: Go 1.26 Language Specification (go1.26.3), https://go.dev/ref/spec, 'Method declarations' makes a method declaration a top-level declaration, so the interface and its implementations CANNOT be declared inside a function body, and the measured region must be a single contiguous span. Hop kind IFACE. type_and_representation, possible_failure, control_flow_effect and allocation_copy_move_borrow_destroy are all resolved from the fragment plus the specification, because the type argument is written explicitly.

hidden_items.checklist_item: H3 -- Overload or dynamic dispatch not locally evident
hidden_items.why: At local site 1 -- the declaration `func maxOf[T cmp.Ordered](a, b T) T { if a > b { return a }; return b }` -- the concrete comparison that runs for `a > b` is not determined by the site: `cmp.Ordered`'s type set contains the integer types, the floating-point types and string, and the frozen toolchain emits materially different code for them (an integer compare, an IEEE-754 compare in which every comparison with NaN is false, and a call to the runtime's byte-wise string comparison). Candidate cardinality >= 2, and the instantiation that selects among them is written at local site 2, which section 0.7 explicitly places outside site 1. Section 1.4's first H3 exclusion does not apply because it requires 'the operand type set ... fixed by the local site', which is exactly what a type parameter leaves open, and no per-candidate equivalence record is possible: the float candidate and the integer candidate differ on the NaN edge. H8 was adjudicated and REJECTED at local site 2 and at the fragment level: the probe's frozen implementation instantiates T only at int32, so no NaN or string edge is reachable in the probe's declared input domain, and a comparison cannot overflow. H1 was adjudicated and REJECTED: the untyped constants 3 and 5 take the written type argument's type, which is section 1.4's third H1 exclusion ('fixing the type of an untyped literal where the reference determines the single resulting type from the local site alone'). H4 and H5 were adjudicated and REJECTED: no allocation is written and measured, and no failure edge exists.

probes.support_reason: Deterministic tie-break answered YES for every numbered sub-requirement. F-1: (1) `type Named interface{ tag() string }` declares an abstract type with one operation returning a text string (Go 1.26 Language Specification (go1.26.3), https://go.dev/ref/spec, 'Interface types'); (2) `A` and `B` are two distinct concrete types implementing it, whose `tag` returns "a" and "b"; (3) `items := []Named{A{}, B{}}` is a single sequence whose DECLARED element type is `Named`, holding one A value and one B value, and the concrete type of an element is not recoverable from that declared element type -- verified, since `items[0].r` or any A-specific member is rejected and a type assertion would be required; (4) `items[0].tag()` calls `tag` on element 0, dispatched at run time through the interface to A's implementation, producing "a". F-2/F-3/F-4: core language only; builds and runs under the frozen recipe, printing a; no extra flag. F-6: no normative prohibition. R10 SELECTION RECORD (frozen tokenizer): CHOSEN form = 73 tokens. The package-level variant (`var items = []Named{A{}, B{}}` and `var first = items[0].tag()`) is 69 tokens, 4 fewer, and is REJECTED under R1, not under R10: sub-requirement (4) asks for the call's result to be PRODUCED as the fragment's result, and a package-level variable initialized before main is not a production. The more expensive form is chosen deliberately. Go 1.26 Language Specification (go1.26.3), https://go.dev/ref/spec, 'Method declarations' makes a method declaration a top-level declaration, so the interface and its two implementations cannot live inside a function body and the measured region must be a single contiguous span at package level.

determinacy_enumeration: FULLY DETERMINED. The interface, both concrete types, both method bodies, the heterogeneous sequence and the dispatching call are all inside the measured fragment; nothing is reached from outside it. Axis outcomes: A1 = copy at every binding; A4 = one interface type, two distinct zero-size struct types and string, all written; A6 = cannot fail -- the index is a constant 0 against a literal of length 2, and the receiver of the dispatched call is the non-nil A{} written in the same fragment; A7 = the dispatch is dynamic in the language, but the dynamic type at this span is fixed by the literal; A8 = the slice literal names its own allocation and the zero-size elements cost nothing; A9 = the callee returns and the function returns. EXCLUDED CLASSES with citation and refutation witness (Rule 1.3.1.e): (a) A6 = 'may trap/panic on a nil interface element' -- EXCLUDED, both elements are written in the literal; refutation witness vnil.go writes `[]Named{nil, B{}}` with the byte-identical call and panics with 'runtime error: invalid memory address or nil pointer dereference', showing that the literal's own elements, not the environment, are what close the class. (b) A4 = A and B are the same type because their underlying types are identical -- EXCLUDED, Go 1.26 Language Specification (go1.26.3), https://go.dev/ref/spec, 'Type definitions' makes a defined type a new, distinct type; refutation witness vab.go writes `var x A = B{}` and is rejected with 'cannot use B{} (value of struct type B) as A value in variable declaration'. (c) A7 = 'the call target may differ between executions' -- Rule 1.4.7 forbids counting mere target variability as a branch in any language, and here the element is pinned by the literal in any case. (d) A8 = 'copy/clone may run user code' or 'destruction may run here' -- NOT REALIZABLE, LOW-B-BY-ABSENCE: Go has no copy constructor, no assignment overload, no destructor and no deinitializer. (e) A1 = move/consume and token substitution (Rule 1.4.8) -- NOT REALIZABLE, LOW-B-BY-ABSENCE.
